name: PCF8563 real-time clock module
description: NXP PCF8563 real-time clock/calendar: seconds to years in BCD with leap-year handling, alarm, countdown timer and a programmable CLKOUT square wave, on a 400 kHz I2C bus at address 0x51. Chip runs on 1.8-5.5 V with the I2C bus active and draws about 0.25 uA when timekeeping. Sold as: HW-689 / HZ-8563 blue PCF8563 RTC module (6-pin header INT, COT, SCL, SDA, GND, VCC; coin-cell holder, no I2C pull-ups), I2C address 0x51.
eli5: A tiny clock that keeps the date and time, even while your board is switched off if a coin cell is fitted.

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output for alarm/timer, open-drain, active LOW. Needs a 10 kOhm pull-up if used; not needed for basic use

pins.name: COT
pins.description: CLKOUT square-wave output (32.768 kHz at power-on), open-drain; not needed for basic use

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, up to 400 kHz. The module has no pull-up: fit 4.7 kOhm to 3.3 V

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain. The module has no pull-up: fit 4.7 kOhm to 3.3 V

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.2-5.5 V (3.3 V recommended with a 3.3 V board)

supplierQuery: PCF8563 RTC module I2C real time clock
buildNotes: Fixed I2C address 0x51 (A2h write / A3h read in 8-bit form); only one PCF8563 per bus.
The HW-689 module has no SDA/SCL pull-ups: fit 4.7 kOhm from each to 3.3 V.
Power VCC from 3.3 V when the board is a 3.3 V ESP32 or Pico: at VCC = 5 V the chip needs SDA/SCL above 0.7 x VDD, which a 3.3 V bus barely reaches.
Read all seven time registers (02h-08h) in one burst; the chip freezes its counters during the access so the fields stay consistent.
Bit 7 of the seconds register (VL) is set at first power-up or after a brown-out: the time is invalid until you set it. Setting the time clears it.
Write control/status 1 (00h) = 0x00 once after power-up: the reset value 0x08 leaves TESTC set.
CLKOUT runs at 32.768 kHz from power-up; write 0x00 to register 0Dh to switch it off and save current.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf8563 import PCF8563

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
rtc = PCF8563(i2c)
rtc.datetime((2026, 12, 31, 23, 59, 57))  # Thursday 31 Dec 2026, 23:59:57
while True:
    y, mo, d, wd, h, mi, s = rtc.datetime()
    print('wd=%d %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d' % (wd, y, mo, d, h, mi, s))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Keeps the time it was set to and rolls over into 2027

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
